note: Independently re-judged from the complete RFC 8654, RFC 4271 Section 6 and every live tagged occurrence, including the prior canonical verdict. Proposed Tested selector is "treats an improper BGP Extended Message as a fatal error"; Gap selector is "follow the error-handling procedures of [RFC4271]"; gap-context Producer is internal/component/bgp/reactor/relay_recovery.go::admitRecovery. The full requirement remains unmet or unproven outside the tested scope; the selectors locate the parent quote and do not turn all imported RFC 4271 procedures into proof. This verdict must not be stamped until the row carries a matching partial marker and every distinct cover has a current native record, including the presently absent positive and negative covers for TestValidateLengthWithMax. The tagged header tables assert exact bad-length Message Header Error/Bad Message Length and within-limit acceptance. Those helper assertions inspect a returned Notification value or no error; they do not observe socket fatal-error procedures, route cleanup or owner lifetime. The real TCP rejection separately sends exact 1/2 with Data 1001 and EOF on a 4097-octet UPDATE without advertised capability 6. TestRFC8654FatalLengthReleasesInstalledRoutes first proves two actual received routes in Adj-RIB-In, Loc-RIB and recipient TCP, then asserts exact fatal notification, EOF, session/timer/encoding-context cleanup, storage removal and both downstream withdrawals. TestRFC8654FatalLengthReelectsAlternateBest proves the preferred route before failure, selects the surviving route with its own exact AS_PATH and NEXT_HOP on post-failure recipient TCP, observes a single Loc-RIB replacement without transient withdrawal, and withdraws the prefix with no survivor. The 4096-octet control retains the same live session, contexts and installed routes, forwards changed MED, and forbids notification/withdrawal. The shared fixture now installs a real terminal next-hop cover in the actual Loc-RIB before reception; it retains the original installed-state barriers and does not stub reachability or cleanup. The coalesced-reader change passes the received UPDATE type only on the pre-establishment FSM-error call; header-length validation and fatal cleanup remain before body/admission handling. Native renewal job-rfc6608-record-renewals-09a8e39e.log records the valid-control clean pass and named red under a whole coalesced-reader break; that red occurs during OPEN acceptance and proves producer dependence, not discrimination of the later fatal-cleanup or owner-lifetime boundary. RFC 4271 Section 6 additionally requires advertising withdrawal or replacement before invalid routes are finally deleted. The current tagged tests explicitly disclaim observing the lifetime of the last invalid-route/advertisement owner. sendBatchedWithdrawals and admitRecovery carry compact departure inventory into outbound work, and forward workers retain their queued references, but final storage/TCP observations would still pass if a different final owner were released prematurely. The existing summary's Proof boundaries already discloses this unresolved lifecycle obligation. Cross-plugin timestamps or requiring TCP delivery before Adj-RIB-In release would assert a different rule. A lifecycle observation or explicit runtime ownership contract, and a narrow fault that breaks that boundary after installation, are still owed. Therefore the prior enforced verdict overstates whole-clause proof; partial preserves the substantial observed fatal-handling behavior without claiming imported ordering.
